migrate.title: Bring your existing set-up across
migrate.description:
We found an existing Smart Irrigation installation. Irrigation Plus can import its configuration — your zones, buckets, schedules, run history and weather settings, including your API key.

Important: leave the old Smart Irrigation integration in place until this finishes. Removing it first deletes its stored API key, which cannot be recovered afterwards.

leftover_legacy_directory.title: The old Smart Irrigation folder is still installed
leftover_legacy_directory.description:
Irrigation Plus now installs to its own folder, but the previous Smart Irrigation folder is still at `{path}`. HACS does not remove it when an integration changes folder, and Home Assistant will load it as a second integration — so you will see two of every sensor.

Delete that folder and restart Home Assistant. Your configuration has already been carried over.

foreign_legacy_install.title: Another irrigation integration shares this folder
foreign_legacy_install.description:
A different `smart_irrigation` integration is installed at `{path}`. That is fine — the two can run side by side, which is the point of the rename.

One thing to know: dashboards using the old `smart-irrigation-zones-card` type now belong to that integration, not this one. Switch them to `irrigation-plus-zones-card`.

legacy_dashboard_cards.title: {count} dashboard card(s) still use the old name
legacy_dashboard_cards.description:
{count} card(s) still refer to `custom:smart-irrigation-zones-card`. They keep working for now, but they will break if you ever install the other `smart_irrigation` integration alongside this one.

This repair repoints them at `custom:irrigation-plus-zones-card`. Dashboards defined in YAML cannot be changed automatically; those are named for you at the end so you can edit them yourself.

confirm.title: Repoint dashboard cards
confirm.description: Update {count} card(s) to the new card type? Your dashboards are saved as new versions, so you can undo this from the dashboard history.

manual.title: Some dashboards must be edited by hand
manual.description:
{changed} dashboard(s) were updated. These could not be, because they are defined in YAML and Home Assistant does not allow them to be written:

{dashboards}

Open each one and replace `{old_type}` with `{new_type}`.

Until you do, this repair will reappear after every restart — the old card type is still in those dashboards.

renamed_entity_ids.title: {count} entity IDs changed in the rename
renamed_entity_ids.description:
The rename changed every entity ID. Your history, statistics and configuration were carried across automatically, and service calls to `smart_irrigation.*` still work for now.

Entity IDs written into your own automations, scripts, templates and dashboards were not changed — nothing in Home Assistant can rewrite those, and a template pointing at an old ID quietly renders `unknown` instead of raising an error.

The full old → new table is saved at `{path}`. Work through it, then dismiss this.
